g.text: Lifespan of UM-HET3 females: maternal allele, B against C

text.style: font-size: 17.04px; font-weight: bold; font-style: italic; font-family: "Arial";

g.text: at one T-age: 3.5 at T20 to 3.6 at T1100 (any T-age to T770 4.3). From 1,000 permutations of lifespans within site

Model: lm(age at death ~ site + cohort + treatment + maternal B dosage, P(BH) + P(BD)), likelihood-ratio test (1 d.f.), as in Danny Arends's ProgressiveMapping.R. UM-HET3 females alive at T; 891 markers (Arends et al. 2026, Supplementary Table 7).
Lifespan of UM-HET3 females: paternal allele, D against H

text.style: font-size: 17.04px; font-weight: bold; font-style: italic; font-family: "Arial";

g.text: at one T-age: 3.3 at T20 to 3.4 at T1100 (any T-age to T770 4.1). From 1,000 permutations of lifespans within site

Model: lm(age at death ~ site + cohort + treatment + paternal D dosage, P(CD) + P(BD)), likelihood-ratio test (1 d.f.), as in Danny Arends's ProgressiveMapping.R. UM-HET3 females alive at T; 891 markers (Arends et al. 2026, Supplementary Table 7).

Mapping: umhet3_maps.R (robwwilliams/BxDLifeSpan). Paternal calls on proximal Chr 1 are biased toward H at UM and UT. A female's paternal X is always H (her father's mother was C3H/HeJ) so the paternal X is not mapped.
